summary: Fully verified Discord OAuth login/signup implementation for the SC Group Finder app. Backend: 6/6 pytest cases pass — /api/auth/discord/login issues a 307 redirect to discord.com/api/oauth2/authorize with correct client_id (1526294227099713556), redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope='identify email'; /api/auth/discord/callback with no code redirects to /login?discord_error=missing_code (and propagates ?error=access_denied); /api/auth/discord/complete rejects bogus JWTs, JWTs with wrong scope, and expired JWTs (all 401 with 'Invalid or expired Discord session'). Frontend: Login page (/login) shows 'CONTINUE WITH DISCORD' button in Discord blue rgb(88,101,242) with 'RSI verification still required for new accounts.' subtext. Clicking the button navigates the browser AT TOP LEVEL to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=...&scope=identify+email — the iframe-breakout fix (<a target='_top'>) works correctly. Register page (/register) shows 'SIGN UP WITH DISCORD' on the standard form. Discord-pending mode (/register?discord=<token>&email=...&discord_username=TestUser) correctly shows the discord-linked-banner ('Linked to Discord as TestUser. Add your RSI handle to finish.'), prefills+disables the email field, hides both password fields (count=0), shows the RSI handle field, and hides the standalone 'SIGN UP WITH DISCORD' button. All requested checks in the review request pass.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 4621 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Should be split into modular routers (auth, discord, contracts, signals, etc.). Not blocking, but flagging for future refactor.
_verify_discord_pending_token correctly enforces scope='discord_pending' — good defense against auth-token abuse.

The Discord callback creates a new user with a random unusable password when no email match found; this is fine, but note the placeholder email 'discord_{id}@starcitizengroupfinder.local' can never receive real notifications — consider marking such accounts explicitly and requiring email confirmation later.
Frontend handleDiscordLogin correctly uses <a target='_top'> with rel='noopener' — this is the correct pattern for breaking out of iframes; verified working on real preview URL.
test_credentials: JWT_SECRET=navcom-dev-secret-key-2025 (used to forge test pending token). Existing admin creds untouched.
seed_data_creation: None. Tests only exercise token-validation error paths on /api/auth/discord/complete — no DB writes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_discord_oauth.py covers all Discord OAuth error paths. Live Discord OAuth completion (real user consent + RSI bio verification) is NOT tested here — would require real Discord authorization + RSI account. Playwright verified the iframe-breakout fix works: clicking the Discord button in a top-level browser context navigates the page to discord.com/oauth2/authorize with all correct query params. When running inside the Emergent preview iframe, the fix uses target='_top' to escape the iframe before navigating.
rca of the issue: Original bug: 'discord.com refused to connect' — Discord sets X-Frame-Options: DENY so it cannot be loaded inside the Emergent preview iframe. Fix (applied by main agent): handleDiscordLogin creates an <a target='_top' rel='noopener'> element pointing to /api/auth/discord/login and clicks it. target='_top' forces navigation to happen in the topmost browsing context, escaping any parent iframe. Verified: clicking the button in Playwright navigated the top-level page to https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=1526294227099713556&...&scope=identify+email — confirming the fix works.
